claims.text: Tuning the active-site electronic structure governs reliable single-phase nanoparticle formation in noble-metal-based HEAs.
Tuning the active-site electronic structure governs enhanced catalytic performance in noble-metal-based HEAs.
A narrow and optimally balanced fdMetal + α·χ̄N distribution produces uniform and optimal adsorption energies for reaction intermediates.
Uniform, optimal adsorption energies lead to superior catalytic activity.
Controlled low-temperature stochastic nucleation leads to stable single-phase material formation.
Low-temperature synthesis inhibits precursor mobility and thereby promotes single-phase formation of pentanary HEA nanoparticles.
Changing HEA elemental composition and component ratios can tune the fdMetal + α·χ̄N descriptor and catalytic behavior.
A targeted pentanary alloy will have a narrower and more optimal descriptor distribution than corresponding ternary or quaternary alloys.
Alloys with fewer elements naturally have broader active-site descriptor distributions.
The fdMetal + α·χ̄N descriptor combines the d-band filling of an active metal center with the average electronegativity of its neighboring atoms.
The fdMetal + α·χ̄N descriptor reliably predicts adsorption energies on noble-metal HEA surfaces across different elements and component ratios.
The complex local chemical environment of multimetallic HEAs electronically perturbs active metal centers.
Interatomic electronic perturbations from multiple constituent metals produce a confined and optimal distribution of adsorption energies.
Uniform adsorption-energy distributions facilitate kinetically controlled formation of a single-phase structure during synthesis.
Intermediate adsorption strengths that are neither too strong nor too weak enhance catalytic activity.
The optimized pentanary HEA will exhibit a narrower adsorption-energy range than the lower-component baseline.
The optimized pentanary HEA will have higher catalytic activity than the lower-component baseline.
The optimized pentanary HEA will have greater catalytic or structural stability than the lower-component baseline.
The hypothesis is limited to low-temperature conditions that restrict large-scale atomic diffusion and precursor mobility.

Failure of the optimized pentanary alloy to show either a statistically significant narrowing of adsorption energies or improved catalytic performance relative to the control is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
